audience.description: An explicitly specified audience's observed or predicted response. Never a universal funniness score.

comic_reading.description: Whether the supplied evidence supports a humorous reading.

values.ambiguous: Two or more readings (including a literal one) remain credible; no main reading is declared.
values.insufficient_context: The reading depends on context that was not supplied.
values.not_supported: The material reads as sincere or literal; no comic reading is supported.
values.supported: A coherent comic reading is supported by evidence in the input or supplied context.

mechanism.description: The relationship that creates the comic effect.

values.absurd_reasoning: Internally consistent logic applied from an absurd premise.
values.ambiguity: A word, phrase or structure supports two readings that the material exploits.
values.callback: A later turn reapplies an element established earlier.
values.exaggeration: Scale is inflated beyond plausibility to make a point.
values.incongruity: Two frames or facts clash in a way the material makes salient.
values.irony: The intended evaluation is opposed to or diverges from the literal one.
values.literalisation: A figurative expression is taken at its literal value.
values.misdirection: The setup steers toward an expectation the continuation overturns.
values.personification: An inanimate thing or abstraction is given human needs or agency.
values.reversal: A role, outcome or evaluation flips relative to what was established.
values.sarcasm: Verbal irony aimed at a target, typically with critical force.
values.self_defeating_logic: An action or statement undermines its own stated purpose.
values.understatement: Scale or emotion is deflated well below what the situation warrants.

register.description: How the material is presented. Acoustic values require acoustic evidence.

values.acoustically_deadpan: Flat vocal delivery. Requires audio evidence.
values.mock_formal: Formal register applied to a trivial matter.
values.textually_understated: Restrained wording in text. Not a claim about vocal delivery.

values.absurdism: Humour from a world that does not obey ordinary sense.
values.meta_humour: Humour about the form of jokes or the act of joking.
values.observational: Draws humour from a recognisable everyday pattern.
values.parody: Imitates a recognisable form or voice for comic effect.
values.roast: Directed, ritualised mockery of a present target.
values.satire: Exposes a real target's failing through ridicule or ironic framing.
values.wordplay: Humour carried mainly by the form or sense of words.

social_function.description: What the humour appears to do in this interaction. Says nothing about the speaker's personality.

values.affiliative: Builds rapport or shared enjoyment without a victim.
values.aggressive: Belittles, mocks or excludes a target.
values.self_directed: Makes the speaker the butt of the joke. Not the psychological construct "self-defeating".
values.self_enhancing: Keeps a humorous perspective on adversity to cope or reframe.
values.unclear: Function cannot be established from the input.

values.distributed_sequence: The effect spreads across several turns or sentences.
values.headline: Headline or title form.
values.meme_caption: Text dependent on an image template.
values.question_answer: Riddle or question followed by an answer.

target.description: What is being mocked or reframed.
